questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a function parameter?

options.A: To store the function’s return value
options.B: To define a variable that receives data when the function is called
options.C: To specify the function’s access level
options.D: To indicate the function’s execution speed

questions.explanation:
A function parameter defines a variable that will receive data (an argument) when the function is invoked. (Source Page: [62])  

---

questions.question: How does a parameter differ from an argument?

options.A: A parameter is the actual value passed; an argument is the variable in the function definition.
options.B: A parameter is a variable in the function definition; an argument is the actual value passed at call time.
options.C: Parameters are only used in class constructors; arguments are used in all functions.
options.D: There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable.

questions.explanation:
Parameters appear in the function’s definition, while arguments are the concrete values supplied during a call. (Source Page: [62])  

---

questions.question: In a UML class diagram, what information is shown in the top compartment?

options.C: The class’s name, centered and in boldface

questions.explanation:
The top compartment contains the class’s name, centered horizontally and in boldface type. (Source Page: [32])  

---

questions.question: Which compartment of a class diagram lists the class’s attributes (data members) in C++?
questions.explanation:
The middle compartment contains the class’s attributes, which correspond to data members in C++. (Source Page: [32])

questions.question: In the GradeBook example, what is the argument passed to the constructor on line 46?

options.C: The string "CS101 Introduction to C++ Programming"
options.D: No argument is passed; the constructor is default.

questions.explanation:
The argument "CS101 Introduction to C++ Programming" is passed to the GradeBook object’s constructor to initialize courseName. (Source Page: [42])

questions.question: If two GradeBook objects are created, how many copies of the data member `courseName` exist?

options.A: One shared copy for both objects
options.B: Two separate copies, one per object
options.D: Three copies – one for each object and one global copy.

questions.explanation:
Every instance of a class contains its own copy of each data member; thus two objects have two copies of `courseName`. (Source Page: [37])

questions.question: Why is the function `displayMessage` called with empty parentheses in the example?

options.A: Because it returns a value that must be ignored
options.B: Because it requires no additional data to perform its task
options.C: Because it is a constructor, not a regular function
options.D: Because the compiler automatically fills in default arguments

questions.explanation:
`displayMessage` does not require additional data, so it is called with empty parentheses. (Source Page: [32])
